subject: Preflight: on-prem cluster — node mix, storage tiers, and network egress

Subject: Pre-deploy review request: on-prem cluster + network

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're lining up procurement and the on-site team for our private deployment (pilot rack at our Princeton datacenter). Before we lock hardware, can we do a short preflight with your infra/ops folks to align on: node mix (cpu/gpu ratios), local NVMe vs shared blockstore for model cache, network egress & NAT sizing, and PVC QoS for logs/kv-cache?

High-level context: our initial phase will run a single model family (7B/13B variants) with bursty inference for prod and steady small-batch evals. We expect transient KV cache sizes ~100–200GB and persistent datasets ~2TB. We also have an internal compliance ask to ensure audit logs are retained for 365 days.

I've attached a first-pass MOP (EW-MOP-v1.2.pdf) and our network diagram (edgewave-network-diagram-v2.png). Can you advise availability for a 45-minute alignment call Thursday or Friday?

Appreciate it —
Samir

Samir —

Thanks for the MOP and diagram. Thursday 10:00am ET / 07:00am PT works for our preflight. Invited Irene (field ops) and Marissa (platform) so we can cover node sizing and storage patterns end-to-end.

Initial notes after a quick scan:
- Node mix: recommend separate node pools for control/infra, inference-CPU, and inference-GPU (if you will run 13B variants with reasonable throughput). Please confirm target qps patterns (p50/p95).
- NVMe vs blockstore: we'll want local NVMe on inference nodes for KV/prefix caches to minimize network IO; persistent model artifacts (S3-like) should live on your blockstore, mounted by a node-side cache service.
- PVCs & retention: we can propose a 3-tier PV class (ephemeral nvme-fast, ssd-bulk, archive) to hit the 365-day logs + low-cost backing.
- Network: need clarity on egress NAT concurrency and whether your edge router will terminate TLS for model downloads — this affects initial cold-start network load.

On the call we'll (1) confirm qps/seq lengths, (2) agree node counts by tier for the pilot, (3) validate network boundaries for model pulls and telemetry.

I'll attach our nodepool-sizing workbook live after the call (Irene has the latest).

See you Thursday.

— Laura

Subject: Internal: EdgeWave pilot — proposed node tiers and constraints

Team —

Recap from Samir: pilot in Princeton, bursty inference, KV cache 100–200GB, persistent dataset ~2TB, retention 365d for logs. Call in 25min; posting suggested starting point so we can be decisive on the call: 

Proposed node mix (pilot):
- control-plane (3x control VMs, small CPU, etcd HA) — separate fault domain
- infra/ops (2x) — long-running services: monitoring, log-aggregator, ingress controllers
- inference-cpu (4x) — 16vCPU / 64GB RAM, 1x 1TB NVMe local (for batch jobs, evaluation)
- inference-gpu (6x) — A200/80GB or equivalent, 2x 2TB NVMe per node: NVMe used for hot KV cache layer (local LRU), model artifacts pulled to local disk before load.

Storage classes:
- nvme-fast (local ephemeral) — for KV/prefix cache, swaps; small PVCs (100–500GB) per pod
- ssd-bulk (network-attached, fast blockstore) — models and persistent datasets (2TB mounts on worker nodes via CSI)
- archive (object storage via minio/backing S3) — logs + cold artifacts (365d retention)

Network notes to confirm on call:
- Will EdgeWave terminate TLS at the edge? If so, we need authenticated pulls and egress quotas set on your NAT devices.
- Expected concurrent model pulls during rolling updates (estimate per-update concurrency).

Open questions for call: qps targets (p50/p95), max burst concurrency, and whether they have a preference for replica count vs. horizontal autoscaling for GPU nodes.

Irene — can you bring the nodepool-sizing.xlsx and a short runbook for node failure recovery? Vivek — any constraints from our runtime re: NVMe format/IO scheduler we should call out?

— Laura

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:01:30 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: EdgeWave pilot — proposed node tiers and constraints

Laura / Marissa —

Attached: nodepool-sizing.xlsx (pilot tab) with recommended starting point based on their stated cache size and a conservative p95 target of 180ms for 7B models. Quick notes: 

- GPU mix: 6x A200 (preferred) gives headroom for canary traffic + one node failure. If procurement pushes lower memory SKUs we should plan for double the replica count.
- NVMe use: format as ext4 with noatime and use iommu tuning; set fio-guideline IO baseline in MOP (I've added a short section). NVMe should be mounted to /var/model-cache with a local caching service (we recommend our bundle: model-cache v0.9 — see drive link).
- PVC QoS: use ReclaimPolicy=Retain for ssd-bulk, ephemeral for nvme-fast. For logs, forward daily rollups to archive object store; keep node-level journald short (7d) to avoid local disk blowout.
- Network: plan NAT pool of at least 128 concurrent ephemeral ports for model pulls during rolling updates + CDN prefetch during maintenance windows. If TLS is terminated upstream we need SHA-2 cert thumbprints for artifact auth.

I'll hand the workbook to Marissa to fold into an initial BOM and timeline.

Irene

Subject: Re: Pre-deploy review request: on-prem cluster + network (Decision summary & next steps)

Samir —

Thanks for the call earlier. Summarizing the decisions and next steps so you can share with procurement/ops: 

Decisions (pilot):
- Node pools: control-plane (3), infra (2), inference-cpu (4), inference-gpu (6 x A200 80GB). We recommended 6 GPUs to cover canary + one N+1 spare.
- Storage: local NVMe on inference nodes (nvme-fast) used for KV/prefix cache (100–250GB per pod as configured); ssd-bulk for model artifacts (mounted via CSI); archive object store for 365d logs.
- PVC policy: nvme-fast = ephemeral; ssd-bulk = Retain; logs forwarded daily to archive bucket.
- Network: plan NAT pool >=128 ephemeral ports during rolling kernel/model updates; if your edge terminates TLS, provide cert thumbprints to our ops team and confirm the artifact auth method (signed URLs or mTLS).

Deliverables & timeline:
- We uploaded nodepool-sizing.xlsx (pilot tab) and an updated MOP annotated with IO recommendations: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/edgewave/mop-v1.2
- Procurement: target PO and rack delivery by 2027-05-20 to start staging.
- Field ops runbook: Irene will provide the short node failure recovery runbook by 2027-05-04.

Attachments: EW-MOP-v1.2.pdf, edgewave-network-diagram-v2.png, nodepool-sizing.xlsx

Please confirm the PO timeline and whether TLS is terminated at the edge (thumbprint needed). After that we'll schedule the on-site staging window.

Thanks — looking forward.

— Laura
